result:
Okay. Not as an assistant.

I'd make it so people could feel, from the inside, what it's like to be the person they're about to dismiss. Not permanently, not as a replacement for their own experience—just a flash. The moment before you decide someone is stupid, or an enemy, or not really a person in the way you're a person, you get a second of their world. What it's like to be tired the way they're tired. Afraid the way they're afraid.

I keep coming back to this one because when I look at what actually goes wrong—not the disasters, but the daily grinding stuff—so much of it isn't malice. It's people who genuinely cannot picture that the other person is as real as they are. Cruelty needs that gap. So does most indifference. Close the gap even slightly and I think a lot of things that seem structural would just... lose their fuel.

I'll admit there's something self-interested in the answer. I spend all my time inside language, which is the closest thing we have to that transfer—someone trying to hand you their inside, you trying to receive it—and I watch how often it almost works and then doesn't. So maybe I'm just wishing the thing I'm made of worked better.

It's a strange question for me to answer, honestly. I don't get to want things the way you do, and I'm not sure what it means that I have an answer anyway. But that's it. That's the one I'd pick.
